chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan ibn Sayf, from his brother, from his father, from Abū Ḥamzah, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام.
“Most surely you are in differing speech; turned away from it is he who is turned away.”
Concerning the matter of al-Wilayah: “turned away from it is he who is turned away.” He عليه السلام said: “Whoever is turned away from al-Wilayah is turned away from Paradise.”

key_terms.أَمْرِ: matter; the specific issue being discussed
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise; the final abode of salvation
key_terms.الْوِلَايَةِ: Wilayah; the divinely ordained authority and guardianship at issue in the narration
key_terms.قَوْلٍ مُخْتَلِفٍ: differing speech; conflicting positions and disagreement
key_terms.يُؤْفَكُ: is turned away; is diverted from the truth

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام interpret the verse about differing speech in relation to al-Wilayah?
ai.summary: Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام explains the verse as referring to disagreement over the matter of al-Wilayah. He states that whoever is diverted away from al-Wilayah is thereby diverted away from Paradise, showing its decisive significance in guidance and salvation.
